BG.10.1.context: Krishna opens chapter 10, on his divine manifestations, speaking out of care for Arjuna.
BG.10.1.english: Listen again, mighty-armed one, to my supreme word, which I will speak to you, who delight in it, because I wish for your good.

school_notes.note: You drink in my words like nectar and delight in them, so I speak further for your good.
Because you delight in hearing of my greatness, I speak of it further, wishing for your good: the birth and growth of devotion to me.
This chapter teaches his manifestations, as objects of meditation.

BG.10.2.context: Krishna says not even gods and sages know his origin, since he is their source.
BG.10.2.english: Neither the hosts of gods nor the great sages know my origin, for I am the source of the gods and of the great sages in every way.

school_notes.note: Neither gods like Brahmā nor sages like Bhṛgu know my power or my origin, since I am their source.
Even the gods and sages, who see beyond the senses, do not know my names, deeds, nature and qualities, because their very knowledge and power come from me.

BG.10.3.context: Krishna says knowing him as unborn and beginningless frees a person from wrongdoing.
BG.10.3.english: One who knows me as unborn and beginningless, the great Lord of the worlds, is undeluded among mortals and is freed from all wrongdoing.

school_notes.note: Since I am the beginning of gods and sages and nothing comes before me, I am unborn and beginningless; one who knows this is freed from all sins.
'Unborn' sets him apart from matter and from bound souls, whose 'birth' is karma-made contact with matter; 'beginningless' sets him apart even from liberated souls.
'Beginningless' means he is the mover and the beginning of everything.

BG.10.4.context: Krishna lists the inner states of beings, all of which arise from him (10.4-10.5).
BG.10.4.english: Understanding, knowledge, freedom from confusion, patience, truthfulness, self-restraint and calm, pleasure and pain, birth and death, fear and fearlessness,

school_notes.note: Understanding is the mind's ability to grasp subtle things; patience is staying unmoved when insulted or struck.
Understanding is the mind's power to discern; patience is keeping the mind unmoved even when there is cause to be upset.
Understanding is deciding what should and should not be done; calm is being established in the Supreme.

BG.10.5.context: Krishna completes his list of inner states, saying all come from him.
BG.10.5.english: non-violence, evenness, contentment, austerity, generosity, fame and infamy: all these different states of beings arise from me alone.

school_notes.note: Non-violence is not harming living beings; contentment is feeling one has enough; generosity is sharing according to one's means.
Contentment is the sense of 'enough'.

BG.10.6.context: Krishna names the ancient sages and Manus, ancestors of all creatures, as born of his mind.
BG.10.6.english: The seven great sages of old and the four Manus, from whom all the creatures of this world descend, were born of my mind and share my nature.

school_notes.note: The seven great sages such as Bhṛgu, and the four Manus known as the Sāvarṇas, were born of my mind, endowed with Viṣṇu's power.
The seven sages of the previous age, born of Brahmā's mind to carry on creation, and the four Sāvarṇika Manus who maintain it; all these creatures are their descendants.
The seven sages are Marīci, Atri, Aṅgiras, Pulastya, Pulaha, Kratu and Vasiṣṭha, as the Mokṣadharma lists; the four Manus are the first ones, beginning with Svāyambhuva.

BG.10.7.context: Krishna says that knowing his glory and power leads to unwavering yoga.
BG.10.7.english: Whoever truly knows this divine glory and power of mine is joined with unwavering yoga; there is no doubt of this.

school_notes.note: Whoever truly knows my glory and my yogic power is joined with unshakeable yoga, the steadiness of right vision.
'Glory' is that everything's origin, existence and activity depend on me; 'power' here is my auspicious qualities. Knowing these truly brings unwavering devotion.

BG.10.8.context: Krishna describes how the wise, knowing him as the source of all, worship him with love (10.8-10.11).
BG.10.8.english: I am the source of all; everything proceeds from me. Knowing this, the wise worship me, filled with love.

school_notes.note: I, the supreme Brahman called Vāsudeva, am the origin of the whole world; knowing this, the wise worship me with deep feeling.
Knowing my natural, unlimited lordship together with my gentleness, beauty and tenderness, the wise worship me with love.
There are some who do worship him in this way.

BG.10.9.context: Krishna describes the shared joy of devotees who speak of him together.
BG.10.9.english: With minds fixed on me and lives given to me, enlightening one another and always speaking of me, they are content and full of joy.

school_notes.note: Their minds are on me and their senses drawn into me, or their very life is me; they teach one another and speak of me, finding contentment and delight.
Unable to live without me, they tell one another of the qualities of mine they have experienced and of my lovely deeds, and find contentment and joy.

BG.10.10.context: Krishna promises the understanding that leads to him to those who love him.
BG.10.10.english: To those who are always devoted and worship me with love, I give the yoga of understanding by which they come to me.

school_notes.note: To those always absorbed, having given up every outward desire, who worship me out of love and not to gain something, I give the yoga of understanding.
To those who long for constant union with me, I give that same yoga of understanding in its mature form, by which they reach me.

BG.10.11.context: Krishna says he dwells in his devotees' hearts and dispels their ignorance with knowledge.
BG.10.11.english: Out of compassion for them, dwelling in their hearts, I destroy the darkness born of ignorance with the shining lamp of knowledge.

school_notes.note: Out of compassion, dwelling in their inner being, I destroy the darkness of delusion born of lack of discernment with the lamp of discerning knowledge.
To favour them, I dwell in their thoughts, revealing my auspicious qualities, and with the shining lamp of knowledge of me I destroy the darkness of past karma that blocks it.

BG.10.12.context: Arjuna responds by acknowledging Krishna as the supreme Brahman (10.12-10.15).
BG.10.12.english: You are the supreme Brahman, the supreme abode, the supreme purifier; the eternal divine Person, the first of the gods, unborn and all-pervading.

school_notes.note: You are the supreme Self, the supreme light, the supreme purifier: the eternal divine Person, the first god, unborn and all-pervading.
You are the one the scriptures call supreme Brahman, supreme light and supreme purifier, as in 'that from which these beings are born'.
'Brahman' means the one who is full, from the root 'bṛh', to grow; 'all-pervading' (vibhu) means existing in many forms.

BG.10.13.context: Arjuna notes that the great sages have all described Krishna this way.
BG.10.13.english: All the sages say this of you, and so do the divine sage Narada, Asita, Devala and Vyasa; and now you tell me yourself.

school_notes.note: Sages like Vasiṣṭha, the divine sage Nārada, Asita, Devala and Vyāsa say this, and you yourself tell me so.

BG.10.14.context: Arjuna affirms his faith in Krishna's words.
BG.10.14.english: I accept as true all that you tell me, Krishna. Neither the gods nor the demons know your manifestation, Lord.

school_notes.note: All this, said by the sages and by you, I take to be true; neither gods nor demons know your origin.
I take all this as plain statement of fact, not mere praise: your unlimited lordship and countless qualities are beyond the knowledge of gods and demons.

BG.10.15.context: Arjuna says only Krishna can truly know himself.
BG.10.15.english: You alone know yourself through yourself, supreme Person, source of beings, lord of beings, god of gods, lord of the world.

school_notes.note: You alone know yourself, the Lord of unsurpassed knowledge, lordship and strength.
You know yourself by your own knowledge alone: creator and ruler of all beings, highest god of the gods.

BG.10.16.context: Arjuna asks Krishna to describe the glories by which he pervades the world (10.16-10.18).
BG.10.16.english: Please tell me fully of your divine glories, by which you pervade these worlds and abide in them.

school_notes.note: Tell me fully of your divine glories, the extensions of your greatness, by which you pervade these worlds.
Only you can reveal your divine glories, the countless ways of governing by which you pervade the worlds as their controller.
'Glories' (vibhūti) are his various manifestations.

BG.10.17.context: Arjuna asks in which forms he should contemplate Krishna.
BG.10.17.english: How may I know you, yogi, by always meditating on you? In what different forms should I think of you, Lord?

school_notes.note: How should I know you through constant meditation, and in which things should you be meditated upon?
As a devotee who wants to meditate on you always, in which beings, besides those you have named, should I think of you?

BG.10.18.context: Arjuna asks to hear more, never tiring of Krishna's words.
BG.10.18.english: Tell me again in detail of your power and your glory, Krishna; for I am never satisfied hearing your nectar-like words.

school_notes.note: Explains the name 'Janārdana': the one who sends the enemies of the gods to hell, or to whom people pray for prosperity and liberation.
Tell me in detail of your creative power and glory, summarised in 10.8; I can never have enough of the nectar of your greatness.
'Janārdana' means the one who is not born and who destroys worldly existence.

BG.10.19.context: Krishna agrees to describe his chief manifestations, since there is no end to them all (10.19-10.42).
BG.10.19.english: Very well, I will tell you of my divine glories, best of the Kurus, but only the principal ones, for there is no end to my extent.

school_notes.note: I will tell you the chief glory in each class; there is no end to my extent.
'Principal' means the most excellent: I will name certain excellent things in the world as my glories.

BG.10.20.context: Krishna begins with his chief manifestation: he is the self within every being.
BG.10.20.english: I am the self, Arjuna, dwelling in the heart of all beings; I am the beginning, the middle and the end of beings.

school_notes.note: I am the inner self in the heart of all beings, always to be meditated upon; he explains 'Guḍākeśa' as one who has conquered sleep, or one with thick hair.
I dwell as the self in the heart of all beings, who are my body; the self of a body is its support, controller and master, as 15.15 says.

BG.10.21.context: Krishna names his manifestations among the gods and the heavenly lights.
BG.10.21.english: Among the Adityas I am Vishnu; among lights, the radiant sun; among the Maruts I am Marichi; among the stars, I am the moon.

school_notes.note: Of the twelve Ādityas, I am the one named Viṣṇu; among lights, the radiant sun.
Of the twelve Ādityas, the twelfth and highest, Viṣṇu, is me.
Derives 'Viṣṇu' from the roots meaning to pervade and to enter.

BG.10.22.context: Krishna continues: he is the finest of the Vedas, of the gods, of the senses, and consciousness itself.
BG.10.22.english: Among the Vedas I am the Sama Veda; among the gods I am Indra; among the senses I am the mind; and in living beings I am consciousness.

school_notes.note: Among the senses I am the mind, which deliberates; in beings I am consciousness, the awareness ever present in body and mind.
The highest of the Vedas, the Sāmaveda, is me; the highest of the senses, the mind, is me.

BG.10.23.context: Krishna names his manifestations among divine beings and mountains.
BG.10.23.english: Among the Rudras I am Shankara; among the yakshas and rakshasas, Kubera, lord of wealth; among the Vasus I am fire; and among peaks, Meru.

school_notes.note: Of the eleven Rudras I am Śaṅkara; of the eight Vasus I am fire.
Of the eleven Rudras I am Śaṅkara; among the yakṣas and rākṣasas, Vaiśravaṇa (Kubera).

BG.10.24.context: Krishna names his manifestations among priests, generals and waters.
BG.10.24.english: Among household priests, know me to be the chief, Brihaspati, son of Pritha; among generals I am Skanda; among bodies of water, the ocean.

school_notes.note: Bṛhaspati, as Indra's priest, is chief among household priests.
The foremost of priests, Bṛhaspati, is me; among generals I am Skanda; among lakes, the ocean.

BG.10.25.context: Krishna names his manifestations among sages, sounds, practices and mountains.
BG.10.25.english: Among great sages I am Bhrigu; among words, the single syllable Om; among sacrifices, the sacrifice of silent repetition; among things that do not move, the Himalaya.

school_notes.note: Among the great sages I am Bhṛgu.
Among words I am the one syllable, Om; among sacrifices, the highest one, japa, repetition of the sacred word.

BG.10.26.context: Krishna names his manifestations among trees, sages, celestial musicians and the perfected.
BG.10.26.english: Among all trees I am the sacred fig; among divine sages, Narada; among the gandharvas, Chitraratha; among the perfected, the sage Kapila.

school_notes.note: Divine sages are gods who became seers by seeing the mantras; the perfected are those born with dharma, knowledge and detachment, like Kapila.
The aśvattha, worshipped among trees; Nārada, the supreme Vaiṣṇava, among divine sages; Kapila, most revered by yogis, among the perfected.
Explains 'Kapila' as the one by whom the world, which is bliss, is protected and dissolved.

BG.10.27.context: Krishna names his manifestations among horses, elephants and humans.
BG.10.27.english: Among horses, know me as Uchchaihshravas, born of the nectar; among lordly elephants, Airavata; and among humans, the king.

school_notes.note: Uccaiḥśravas, king of horses, arose when the ocean was churned for nectar.
'Born of the nectar' describes Airāvata too; among people, I am the king.

BG.10.28.context: Krishna names his manifestations among weapons, cows, the forces of procreation and serpents.
BG.10.28.english: Among weapons I am the thunderbolt; among cows, the wish-granting cow; of procreators I am Kandarpa, the god of love; among serpents I am Vasuki.

school_notes.note: The thunderbolt, made from the bones of Dadhīci; the wish-granting cow of Vasiṣṭha.
Among cows, the divine Surabhi; I am Kandarpa, the cause of procreation; among single-headed serpents, Vāsuki.

BG.10.29.context: Krishna names his manifestations among serpents, water beings, ancestors and those who rule.
BG.10.29.english: Among the nagas I am Ananta; among the beings of the waters, Varuna; among the ancestors, Aryaman; and among those who keep order, Yama.

school_notes.note: Ananta, king of the nāgas; Varuṇa, king of the water deities; Aryaman, king of the ancestors.
Nāgas are many-headed serpents; among those who punish, I am Yama, son of Vivasvat.

BG.10.30.context: Krishna names his manifestations among demons, reckoners, beasts and birds.
BG.10.30.english: Among the daityas I am Prahlada; among those who count, I am time; among beasts, the lion; and among birds, Garuda, son of Vinata.

school_notes.note: Prahlāda among the descendants of Diti; among those who reckon, I am time; among beasts, the lion or the tiger.
Among those who calculate with intent to harm, I am time, which is death.

BG.10.31.context: Krishna names his manifestations among purifiers, warriors, sea creatures and rivers.
BG.10.31.english: Among purifiers I am the wind; among those who bear weapons, Rama; among sea creatures, the makara; and among rivers, the Ganga.

school_notes.note: Among those who bear weapons, Rāma, son of Daśaratha.
Here Rāma's bearing of weapons is itself the glory named, since Rāma is the Lord himself.
'Rāma' means the one who is bliss, complete, and in whom the world delights.

BG.10.32.context: Krishna says he is the source, sustainer and end of all creation, and the highest knowledge.
BG.10.32.english: Of creations I am the beginning, the end and the middle, Arjuna; of sciences, the knowledge of the self; and of those who debate, I am reasoned argument.

school_notes.note: Here the whole of creation is meant, not only living beings as in 10.20; among sciences, knowledge of the self, which leads to liberation.
I am the creator in every creation, the destroyer in every dissolution, and the sustainer in between.

BG.10.33.context: Krishna names his manifestations among letters and words, and as endless time.
BG.10.33.english: Among letters I am the letter A; among compounds, the pairing compound. I alone am unending time; I am the creator, facing in all directions.

school_notes.note: The letter A is the source of all sounds, as the Aitareya says; the pairing (dvandva) compound is best because both its parts are equally important.

BG.10.34.context: Krishna names himself as death and as the source of what is to come, and as qualities such as fame, memory and patience.
BG.10.34.english: I am all-devouring death, and the origin of all that is yet to be; among the feminine, I am fame, fortune, speech, memory, intelligence, steadfastness and forbearance.

school_notes.note: Death is of two kinds, one that takes wealth and one that takes life; the one that takes life, or the Lord who takes everything at dissolution, is me.
I am the death that takes all life, and the coming into being of what is yet to be; among women, I am fortune, fame, speech, memory, intelligence, steadiness and patience.

BG.10.35.context: Krishna names his manifestations among chants, metres, months and seasons.
BG.10.35.english: Among the Sama chants I am the Brihat Saman; among metres, the Gayatri; among months I am Margashirsha; and among seasons, flower-bearing spring.

school_notes.note: Among metres, I am the verse in the Gāyatrī metre.
Among the seasons, I am spring, the maker of flowers.

BG.10.36.context: Krishna says he is present even in gambling, as well as in victory, resolve and goodness.
BG.10.36.english: Of cheats I am gambling; I am the brilliance of the brilliant. I am victory, I am resolve, and I am the goodness of the good.

school_notes.note: I am the gambling, with dice and the like, of those who cheat; the victory of victors, the resolve of the resolute, the goodness of those in sattva.
Among the means cheats use, I am the game of dice; in the noble, I am greatness of mind.

BG.10.37.context: Krishna names himself among his own clan, Arjuna among the Pandavas, and Vyasa among sages.
BG.10.37.english: Among the Vrishnis I am Vasudeva; among the Pandavas, Arjuna; among sages I am Vyasa; and among poets, the poet Ushanas.

school_notes.note: Among the Yādavas I am Vāsudeva, this very friend of yours; among the Pāṇḍavas, Dhanañjaya, yourself.
Here being Vasudeva's son is itself the glory named.
'Vāsudeva' is the one who covers all, makes all dwell, and dwells in all, as the Mokṣadharma says.

BG.10.38.context: Krishna names himself as punishment, statecraft, silence and wisdom.
BG.10.38.english: Of those who restrain, I am the rod of punishment; of those who seek victory, I am statecraft; of secrets I am silence; and of the wise I am wisdom.

school_notes.note: The rod that subdues the unruly; statecraft for those who want to win; silence among secret things.
The punishment of those who break rules; the strategy that brings victory; silence in keeping secrets; and the knowledge of the wise.

BG.10.39.context: Krishna sums up: he is the seed of all beings, and nothing exists without him (10.39-10.42).
BG.10.39.english: And whatever is the seed of all beings, that am I, Arjuna; nothing, moving or unmoving, could exist without me.

school_notes.note: Summing up: nothing moving or unmoving exists without me; anything without me would be empty, without a self.
I am the seed of every being in every state; no being could exist without me present as its self (10.20).
There is nothing that could exist without me; he cites the Mokṣadharma's names for the Lord, such as 'infinite'.

BG.10.40.context: Krishna says his glories are endless and what he has named is only a sample.
BG.10.40.english: There is no end to my divine glories, scorcher of enemies; what I have said is only a brief indication of their extent.

school_notes.note: No one can state or know the full extent of the divine glories of the Lord, the self of all; this was only a part.
My auspicious glories are endless; I have described them briefly, through certain examples.

BG.10.41.context: Krishna says all that is glorious or powerful comes from a spark of his splendour.
BG.10.41.english: Whatever is glorious, prosperous or powerful, know that it springs from a spark of my splendour.

school_notes.note: Whatever has glory, prosperity or vigour, know it as arising from a part of my splendour.
Whatever has lordship, radiance, wealth or energy for good undertakings arises from a fraction of my splendour, my power to prevail.
Viṣṇu and his other forms are the Lord himself; other beings merely possess his splendour, as the Paiṅgi supplements say.

BG.10.42.context: Krishna closes chapter 10: the whole world rests on a single fraction of his being.
BG.10.42.english: But what use is all this detailed knowledge to you, Arjuna? I stand supporting this entire world with a single fraction of myself.

school_notes.note: What use is this partial knowledge? Hear it completely: I support this whole world with a single part of myself.
What need for so much? This whole world, conscious and non-conscious, in every state, stands within one fraction of my greatness, never going beyond my will.
This stresses what matters most; it does not mean what was said before is useless.
